title: PR cleanup + small automation ideas (scratchpad)
content:
Quick context:
- Post-merge churn has been creeping up on small refactor PRs. Lots of manual follow-ups: updating docs, adding small tests, and (ugh) undoing accidental whitespace changes that slip through when reviewers approve quickly.
- This is my personal scratchpad for a few lightweight automation ideas + a manual checklist I want to try for the next 2 weeks of reviews. Not an RFC, just notes to try in my local workflow and a couple of tiny scripts to prototype.

What I see repeatedly (examples):
- PRs that refactor a codepath but miss adding unit/regression tests for a previously failing edge case (e.g., tokenization corner-case in serving runtime).
- Small docs (CHANGELOG/upgrade notes) omitted when API surface changes slightly (arg name rename, default config change).
- Formatting-only noise mixed with real changes (makes blame noisy and CI slower).
- Repeated TODO comments left in code after merge.

High-level goals for automation: (keep minimal scope)
1) Detect pure-formatting commits/files and suggest splitting or squashing with rationale.
2) Post-merge automated checklist reminder (bot posts to PR or Slack) for owner with items: add tests, update changelog, update SDK samples.
3) One-click small-PR backfill generator: starter test + minimal changelog snippet + PR template prefilled.
4) Pre-merge light heuristic to flag refactors that change public API surfaces (function signatures, endpoint names).

Tiny scripts/prototypes to try (low-effort):
A) changed_files_summarizer.py (python)
- Input: git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD
- Output: categorize files into: tests, docs, src, formatting-only (via diffstat: e.g., >80% whitespace changes).
- If all changes are formatting-only, print a suggestion: 'Consider splitting formatting from feature changes' and add a suggested commit message to help author.

Pseudo:
# rough idea
# files = run('git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD')
# for f in files: stats = git_diffstat(f) -> {insertions, deletions, whitespace_changes}
# if whitespace_changes/total > 0.8 => formatting-only file

B) post_merge_checklist_bot (github action or simple lambda)
- Trigger: push to main with label "merged-from-pr" OR on PR merge event.
- Action: read PR description, look for keywords (test:, changelog:, sdk-sample:). If keywords missing, post a comment to the author with buttons/links: 'Create test PR (template)', 'Add changelog snippet', 'Open SDK sample draft'.
- MVP: comment with checklist + links to templates in repo.

C) public_api_change_detector (static heuristic)
- Run fast AST diff for python/ts files to detect renamed functions/classes in exported modules or changed function signatures.
- If flagged, mark PR as needs-api-review.

Manual checklist (to use while reviewing):
- [ ] Does this change affect public-facing stable APIs? (search exports and clients)
- [ ] Are there unit tests for the key control flows? If not, add a focused test (happy path + edge case)
- [ ] Changelog note needed? If making user-impacting change, add short blurb and add to changelog/next-release.md
- [ ] SDK samples / examples updated? If not, add TODO in PR description and opt to file follow-up
- [ ] Any new TODOs introduced? If so, comment and require a follow-up task or tie to an issue
- [ ] Formatting noise isolated? If not, ask author to split or rebase

Follow-ups and prioritization (me):
- P0 (this week): prototype changed_files_summarizer.py and wire as local git hook + simple GitHub action printing output as PR comment.
- P1 (next): post_merge_checklist_bot using existing templates from /docs/automation/templates. Keep message minimal to avoid noise.
- P2: prototype public_api_change_detector for python modules only. If hit rate low, iterate with SRE/serving runtime team to define what counts as "public".

Edge cases / risks:
- Bot spam: we must be conservative. For post-merge checklist, only notify if PR author opted-in or if PR touched >1 files or touched code paths with >N users.
- False positives on API detector: many internal helpers are imported across packages; need team-owned whitelist.
- Over-automation encourages authors to ignore comments; make suggestions actionable: provide templates and a one-click create-PR link.

Notes on templates (sketches):
- Test template: small pytest skeleton with parametrized cases and example fixtures used across repo. Keep tests fast (<2s).
- Changelog snippet: markdown snippet with 'user-impact: low|medium|high' field + short description. Author fills rating.
- Backfill PR generator: prefill title "backfill: add test + changelog for PR #NNN", include linked files and suggested test scaffold.

Short-term experiment plan (2 weeks):
- Week 1: implement changed_files_summarizer and run on last 200 merged PRs to measure prevalence of formatting-only + missing tests. Collect metrics: percent of PRs with >1 formatting-only file, percent missing tests where code coverage decreased.
- Week 2: roll out GitHub action to annotate new PRs in my team, get opt-in from 3 reviewers. Measure author response rate and whether suggestions led to follow-ups within 7 days.

Questions for team (to ask in #eng-reviews):
- Would folks find post-merge checklist helpful or annoying? Thoughts on opt-in vs opt-out?
- Are there existing label conventions we should reuse (e.g., "needs-changelog", "api-change")?
- Who should own the whitelist for public API detection? Propose: owning teams for the top-level packages.

Random TODOs I will do next: 
- Draft a 1-page proposal (1 slide) for eng-reviews summarizing the experiment and expected telemetry.
- Build initial changed_files_summarizer prototype and push to /tools/pr-helper/ with a README.
- Try it locally on PR #4128 branch (linked above) and capture output in a sample comment.

Freeform closing notes: 
- Keep the initial scope tiny. The worst outcome is a noisy bot that ends up ignored. The best outcome is a few repeatable nudges that reduce post-merge cleanup by making it trivial to add the missing bits.
- If this works, next wave could integrate with Redwood Console to surface a "post-merge action" checklist in the Rollouts dashboard (later, LLC stuff).
